transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-05
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes (recording paused briefly at ~00:47)
Location: Zoom
Recording: https://redwood-recordings.example/2025-03-05-galvanic
Attendees: Alex Ramos (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Mike Chen (CTO - Galvanic), Sarah Lopez (Head of AI - Galvanic), James Ortiz (Infra Lead - Galvanic)

Summary:
Quick scoping workshop to align on POC success criteria (latency/throughput/cost), workload sizing for burn-rate estimates, benchmark plan (hosted vs dedicated), and timeline for a 2-week POC. Customer emphasized data residency and encryption requirements; infra lead flagged network egress limitations for hosted.

Topics covered:
- Success criteria and acceptable SLOs (p95, p99 latency, throughput targets)
- Representative workload and token profiles for bench runs
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (cost, latency, ops)
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs, VPC peering)
- Pilot timelines, decision gating, and next steps

Transcript body (timestamps approximate; transcription imperfect in places):
[00:00] Alex Ramos: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. mike, sarah, james, we really appreciate you pulling time. we wanted to run through a compact workshop to nail down the POC success criteria and what hosting mode you want to test first.
[00:28] Mike Chen: Yeah thanks Alex. quick context — we're trying to add an in-app assistant for our B2B portal, goal is 95th percentile response under, uh, low-200s ms and peaking at about 50 QPS for search-like gen. long-term we might need up to 200 QPS but pilot smaller.
[01:03] Priya Kapoor: cool, so just to clarify, 95p target low 200ms for what token size? are we talking median payload ~ 128 tokens or full 512 prompts?
[01:18] Sarah Lopez: typical user prompt is 60–120 input tokens, output target ~120 tokens. worst-case 512 but that's rare. our acceptance criteria for POC is p95 < 150ms for 128-token outputs, but we can loosen to 200ms if cost is prohibitive.
[01:46] James Ortiz: couple constraints — our platform sits in eu-west region for customers in EU, and we have a hard requirement that no PII leaves our VPC without encryption and managed keys. hosted is okay if it supports VPC peering or private egress, otherwise we'll need dedicated or private.
[02:15] Alex Ramos: got it. Redwood Dedicated supports reserved pools with VPC peering and private endpoints; Hosted can do regional tenancy and we can arrange private network paths but may add infra routing work. we can also show private on-prem if required, though that's heavier.
[02:44] Speaker 1 (unclear): can we also talk about cost per 1M tokens to compare?
[02:52] Priya Kapoor: yes, we should compare token-based hosted price vs hourly reserved cost amortized. for example for your traffic profile with 50 QPS and average 240 tokens per request that maps to roughly X million tokens per day — we'll calculate exact burn with your logs.
[03:20] Mike Chen: X? (laughs) yeah we can provide logs; expect bursts in US business hours but EU is primary. we'll share 48 hours of traffic.
[03:36] Alex Ramos: great. success criteria that came up so far — p95 <150ms for 128-token median flow, availability >99.5% during the pilot window, and cost target of less than $Y per 1k requests (we'll quantify once we see logs). any other must-haves?
[03:59] Sarah Lopez: we need audit logs for each request for compliance, and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). SOC2 report is a plus.
[04:20] Priya Kapoor: Redwood Console has per-token tracing and request-level logs; we can deliver audit export into your SIEM. KMS integration we support — we do have an HSM option for Private installs. i'll flag compliance follow-up.
[04:41] James Ortiz: network egress is the stick — if hosted needs to route traffic out to public internet, we can't allow that for EU customers.
[04:52] Alex Ramos: understoood — our Dedicated and Private modes can avoid public egress, and we can show a quick diagram. we'll include that in the artifact pack.
[05:10] Mike Chen: timeline question — what's realistic to get a 2-week POC running where we can measure burn? we have infra people but limited windows.
[05:22] Priya Kapoor: typical flow — 1) instrument logs and send sample payloads (2–3 days), 2) Redwood runs bench and tuning (3–5 days), 3) customer validates (2–3 days). So about 10 business days. If we parallelize setup and bench we can hit 7–10 days.
[05:47] Sarah Lopez: we need that within our quarter (end of March) to make an April decision. so tight but could work.
[05:58] Alex Ramos: we'll target bench start week of March 10th then, assuming we get logs by March 7th.
[06:12] [Timestamp jump - recording paused briefly]
[06:40] Priya Kapoor: ok, workload sizing — james, can you outline current request size and token distribution? we want percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and average sequence lengths so we can configure KV cache warmup and batching.
[06:56] James Ortiz: sure, current query mix — 60% short lookups (~40 tokens), 30% medium (~150 tokens), 10% long (~450 tokens). daily active users about 18k, peak concurrent requests around 120, but we only need the assistant on specific pages which reduces effective qps. i'll share histogram.
[07:25] Priya Kapoor: good. for benching we'll run representative synthetic traffic reflecting that mix and a small test of long tails to measure tail latency. caching helps a lot for repeated prefixes; we'll include tests with and without prefix caching.
[07:41] Mike Chen: what's the expected overhead for KV cache in Dedicated vs Hosted? is there any difference in measurable latency?
[07:53] Priya Kapoor: not much functionally — the runtime's caching mechanism is the same, but Dedicated gives you local cache locality on pinned GPUs which reduces inter-node fetches. Hosted might warm a shared cache across customers but we can configure customer-specific cache sizes on Dedicated/Private for better tail behavior.
[08:15] Alex Ramos: another trade is quantization/accuracy. we can test lower precision models on Dedicated which can save costs with minimal accuracy loss. Redwood Optimize can run a quick quality regression against your eval set.
[08:35] Sarah Lopez: yes, we want to preserve our answer accuracy — please include eval metrics (ROUGE or custom scoring) in bench outputs. we don't want a 15% drop in quality for a 30% cost save.
[08:52] Priya Kapoor: absolutely — we'll run A/B with original FP16 model and int8/4 quant variants and report delta. we'll also surface inference throughput curves.
[09:05] [10min marker - side discussion about infra procurement timelines]
[09:14] Mike Chen: procurement will want a clear SLA and an exit strategy if we need to move from hosted to dedicated mid-pilot — how does Redwood handle migrations?
[09:28] Alex Ramos: we provide model pinning and blue/green rollouts. migration from Hosted to Dedicated typically involves a controlled rollout of the same model artifact to the dedicated pool and switching traffic via routing policy; can be done with minimal downtime in practice. we'll prepare an example runbook.
[09:46] James Ortiz: any data transfer windows/costs for moving model caches or big KV stores between environments?
[09:56] Priya Kapoor: model artifacts are generally a few GBs depending on weights; we can snapshot KV caches but it's often faster to rebuild warm cache during initial ramp. we'll note estimated egress.
[10:15] Mike Chen: regarding costs — if we reserve Dedicated capacity, what's a typical commit for a POC? we don't want to overcommit.
[10:26] Alex Ramos: for a POC we recommend a short reserved window with burst capacity — for example a small 4-GPU pool with autoscale throttles to simulate production. pricing can be monthly pro-rata; for POC we do trial pricing and credits in many cases. we'll put the numbers in the spreadsheet.
[10:48] Sarah Lopez: curious about observability — we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency drilldowns.
[10:58] Priya Kapoor: Redwood Console provides route dashboards, token cost breakdown and trace capture. we'll give you a demo link and sample dashboard config.
[11:12] [11:20] Speaker 2 (Generic): can Redwood support SAML/SSO + RBAC for our internal teams?
[11:27] Alex Ramos: yes, SAML and SCIM provisioning supported, role mapping to restrict model deploy permissions; we'll attach the SSO integration doc.
[11:36] James Ortiz: what about audit trail retention? we need logs kept for 13 months for compliance. what's the retention policy?
[11:46] Priya Kapoor: default retention is 90 days, enterprise add-on can extend to 12+ months. for Private you control retention entirely. we'll list options and pricing.
[12:05] Mike Chen: okay, good. let's talk about benchmarks specifics — Priya, what's the bench harness you'll run?
[12:13] Priya Kapoor: we'll use an open harness based on wrk-style generator that supports multi-client streams and sequence-length awareness. for model we'll run the verified open model from Redwood catalog that matches your accuracy baseline, plus a quant variant. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost-per-1k-requests estimated.
[12:40] Sarah Lopez: can we get raw outputs for quality scoring? we want to run our internal scorer.
[12:48] Priya Kapoor: yes, we can export raw predictions and metadata, and you can run your scorer over them. we'll sanitize for PII as needed.
[12:58] [12:58] Alex Ramos: logistics — we need payloads, test accounts, and a window for bench. james, you said you'll share histograms and 48h logs. will that be anonymized?
[13:12] James Ortiz: yes will scrub user ids, keep timings. security team will confirm but it's standard.
[13:22] Mike Chen: regarding private deployment — if we end up requiring on-prem, how long is lead time? we may not need that now but want to know.
[13:33] Alex Ramos: on-prem private deployments are typically 6–10 weeks for initial install and validation depending on footprint and compliance gating. Dedicated (customer-dedicated cloud pools) is much faster — usually days to a couple weeks.
[13:51] Sarah Lopez: okay that's useful.
[14:00] Priya Kapoor: one more note — we'll include microbench for cold start and KV cache warmup behavior; those are real-world pain points for your long-tail cases.
[14:12] Mike Chen: if we see the p95 close but p99 spikes, is Redwood able to do tail mitigation?
[14:21] Priya Kapoor: yes, tail mitigation via request routing to overprovisioned hot nodes, and we can pin a small pool for critical requests. also batching thresholds tuned to preserve tail latency.
[14:36] [15:00] Customer questions about compliance details and SOC2
[15:10] Alex Ramos: we have a current SOC2 report and can sign an NDA to share more. for KMS we support AWS KMS integration and bring-your-own-key via our Private offering.
[15:28] Sarah Lopez: perfect. procurement will want that in the packet.
[15:36] [side chatter about calendar invites]
[16:00] Priya Kapoor: to be practical, i'll outline the bench runs we propose:
- Run A (hosted, regional eu-west) with private endpoint (if network permitted): simulate 72-hour run capturing burst behavior.
- Run B (dedicated reserved 4-GPU pool): same traffic, measure delta.
- Run C (dedicated + quantized model): test throughput/cost tradeoff.
Each run will produce latency percentiles, GPU util, tokens/sec, and quality deltas.
[16:42] Mike Chen: that sounds good. for Run A we might have a 'no-public-egress' requirement; can Redwood wire a private link?
[16:51] Alex Ramos: yes we'll include network diagram and whether we need peering or a private egress appliance.
[17:05] James Ortiz: what about data residency if we have EU-only customers — can hosted EU region guarantee no US routing?
[17:15] Alex Ramos: yes, we can pin region and provide routing policies; we'll validate network routes during bench.
[17:30] [17:40] Speaker 3 (transcription glitch): pvk.. private?
[17:45] Priya Kapoor: yep private on-prem is fallback if regulatory or latency needs force it. but it's heavier.
[17:55] Mike Chen: cost sensitivity — we want to see per-request cost in each mode.
[18:03] Priya Kapoor: we'll produce a per-1k-requests cost estimate factoring in reserved GPU hours, amortized model memory, and token processing. remember hosted uses per-token pricing, dedicated amortizes through reserve.
[18:25] Mike Chen: ok, and what slack for scaling? we have spiky loads.
[18:32] Alex Ramos: Dedicated autoscaling can be configured with burst pools and rate limits; Hosted has elastic scaling but we should test burst behavior in bench to see cold spin-up.
[18:47] Sarah Lopez: Anything else we should cover?
[18:52] James Ortiz: logging integration — can you ship logs to our SIEM (splunk)?
[18:58] Priya Kapoor: yes, we support Splunk/Datadog exports and raw log dumps.
[19:10] [19:20] Quick recap from Alex
[19:21] Alex Ramos: recap — deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet + pricing scenarios, bench scripts from Priya, sample dashboard and SSO docs, and network diagram for private endpoints. timeline: logs by 3/7, bench week of 3/10, initial bench results by 3/17. next meeting: bench kickoff prep on 3/9 — we'll send invite.
[19:49] Mike Chen: sounds good. we'll try to get logs and histogram by 3/7.
[19:56] Sarah Lopez: we'll review evaluation metrics and send our scoring script.
[20:03] Alex Ramos: perfect. any final blockers?
[20:08] James Ortiz: none immediate, security wants SOC2 and KMS notes but that's normal.
[20:14] Alex Ramos: ok thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts.
[20:20] [End of substantive discussion, casual sign-off, meeting wraps at ~17:02 PST]
